title: Yankees, Rays fans guide with matchups, scouting reports, prediction
description: The New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays are playing a best-of-five American League Division Series.
fullText:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The Rays beat out the Yankees for first in the AL East and won more games than anyone in the league with one of the lowest payrolls playing an entertaining throwback style of aggressive baseball. They have three stars at the top of their lineup. They have a .300 hitter in the middle who can fly.

They bunt for hits, squeeze runners home and move runners better than anyone. Their rotation and bullpen are deep. Their record in one-run games was the best in the majors.

The Rays have the Yankees respect.

The Yankees also think they're the better team heading into a postseason showdown that seemed inevitable, a best-of-five Division Series between the two best teams in the league.

"At the end of the day, I think we played Tampa pretty well this year and I think we're in a good spot," Yankees ace Cam Schlittler said.

The Rays won the season series 7-6, but the Yankees feel they're peaking at the right time with their four aces finally all healthy at the same time.

They'll all be unleashed on the Rays. Gerrit Cole will start Saturday night's Game 1 at Tropicana Field, Schlittler will go Game 2, then the Yankees will go to their lefties when the series moves to New York with Carlos Rodon probably starting Game 3 and Max Fried pitching Game 4 if there's no sweep.

The Yankees' Division Series roster will be deeper than the 26-man squad that just swept the Red Sox in a Wild Card Series with 9-0 and 9-2 romps. Ryan Weathers is off the IL and available out of the bullpen, but Aaron Judge still isn't return to return from his Grade 2 calf strain.

The Yankees' one change from their their Wild Card Series roster was adding Weathers for an 11th pitcher and dropping infielder/outfielder Amed Rosario.

Second baseman Jazz Chisholm guaranteed the Yankees will win the series and Schlittler doubled down with "why would I disagree?"

The captain is also confident, regardless of his status.

"The Rays, they've got everything," Judge said. "It's a tough opponent. We're up in the task. We saw them all year. We had our battles, and we're just happy for the opportunity."

Here is a fans' guide to the Yankees-Rays Division Series with a look at how the teams match up and position-by-position scouting reports from an MLB scout:

He didn't play against the lefty in Game 1, then he comes out in Game 2 and gets a couple hits with a walk. I remember watching Wells in the Fall League after he was drafted in the first round because of his bat. Well, he proved me wrong. He does a good job behind the plate. The Rays getting Hicks from Miami added another big threat to a lineup that was very top heavy with Diaz, Aranda and Caminero hitting one, two, three. Hicks is a decent catch-and-throw receiver, too. This was a big get for Tampa because they've never had a catcher who can hit. Hicks brings a lot of offense. He's the full package."

He looks for certain lanes. If the pitch isn't in that zone, he won't swing until he gets to two strikes. That's his kryptonite right there. I'd pitch around him every time he's up. Let Rice get himself out swinging at a bad pitch or walk him. Let somebody else beat you. If the other guys beat me, so be it. Diaz is a clutch hitter who has the ability to control the strike zone. This guy knows his game as a hitter. He has power, but he doesn't try to hit homers."

They don't have anyone like Headrick, but you better believe they'll use all of them this series to try neutralizing all those left-handed hitters in the Yankees lineup. Booser has been effective, but he's more of a touch-and-feel guy. He's not going to strike Ben Rice out in a big spot. Another thing, all of Tampa's left-handed relievers are prone to mistakes left over the plate, especially Matz. If they do that, Tampa's in trouble."

Yankees: Paul Goldschmidt (.252, 18 HR, 52 RBI); CF Trent Grisham (.211, 18 HR, 59 RBI); C Ali Sanchez (.244, 1 HR, 8 RBI, .577 OPS), Anthony Volpe (.245, 3 HR, 28 RBI, .658 OPS).

Scout's take: "The Yankees have power, athleticism and some guys who can play different positions on their bench. Aaron Boone will be able to force Kevin Cash into some moves that he really doesn't want to make because the Yankees have more of a surplus off the bench."

Yankees: Aaron Boone (970-575; 8 playoff berths, 1 pennant, 9th season).

Scout's take: "I've been a big Aaron Boone fan since he was in college at USC. I liked his game and his makeup. From the games I've watched, I think Boone has more leeway to manage with his head than he did in past seasons. Tampa has to play that way because they don't have the power that the Yankees and a lot of other clubs do. I think there's some micromanaging there with Cash because of all this inundated analytics BS that Tampa does. It works for them, but they have not brought home a world championship."

title: Report Shows Why NY Giants & Lions Avoided Big Mistake By Losing Joey Porter Jr. Trade Sweepstakes
description: While some New York Giants and Detroit Lions fans hoped their teams made a trade for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey […]
fullText:
While some New York Giants and Detroit Lions fans hoped their teams made a trade for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., it looks like they avoided a big mistake, based on opinions from around the NFL.

The Steelers have had to deal with the Porter Jr. cloud hanging over the team for months, as the disgruntled three-year veteran apparently faked a back injury until the team gave him the contract extension he wanted or traded him.

Well, the latter came this week when the Steelers sent the corner to the Dallas Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder. Following the trade, fans from teams that didn't get the talented CB wondered why their teams couldn't pull the trigger on a similar deal.

However, there are "many around" the NFL who feel that it was a good decision by teams like the Giants and Lions. "Many around the league believed Dallas overpaid, based largely on the belief that teams don't view Porter as a top-tier corner," The Athletic's Jonathan Jones claims.

There is no doubt that Porter Jr. would have made the Giants' and Lions secondary better. Especially since both teams need help in their secondaries right now. He is one of the better corners in the AFC, and you can never have enough reliable play in that part of the defense.

However, the 26-year-old has never earned year-end Pro Bowl and All-Pro honors. But he wants to be paid like an elite cornerback in his next contract. Something the team that knows him better than anyone- the Steelers- balked at. It is one thing to give up a lot of money. It is another to give up valuable picks and money for a player that isn't a Pro Bowler (yet).

Jones notes that the 2027 NFL Draft class is projected to be very good. So that means a sixth-rounder next year is better than most years. In 2028, the Steelers will get a second-round pick. That is a spot in the draft where franchises can land high-level talent. It is why many around the NFL believe the Cowboys once again overpaid in a trade, especially since they still need to re-sign him.

title: New York Liberty face the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the WNBA semifinals
description: — Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty have been in this spot often in the last few seasons.New York will be making its third appearance in the semifinals of the WNBA playoffs in the past four years when the Liberty play the Atlanta Dream on Sunday in Game 1 of the best-of-five series.
fullText:
NEW YORK (AP) — Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty have been in this spot often in the last few seasons.

New York will be making its third appearance in the semifinals of the WNBA playoffs in the past four years when the Liberty play the Atlanta Dream on Sunday in Game 1 of the best-of-five series.

"Experience in the playoffs definitely matters," Stewart said Friday before practice. "There's so many things (during a longer series) that you have to stay focused on the end goal."

That end goal would be reaching the WNBA Finals and trying to win a second title in three seasons.

"With this group, for the majority of us, (we've) been in this type of series, where it's not getting too high or too low is the huge important part," Stewart said. "And what we did in the first round is great — we're happy to be here — but that wasn't a goal for our season to get out of the first round."

New York was dominant in the first round while sweeping the Minnesota Lynx, becoming the first No. 8 seed to eliminate a No. 1 seed in the league's 30-year history.

"The approach that we're having in these playoffs is pretty much where you want to be," Stewart added. "We're the ones that are staying poised, staying under control at all times. But we're gonna be aggressive for the full 40 minutes, and if you want something, you're gonna have to go through us to get it."

Atlanta is the newcomer to this round, advancing this far for the first time since 2018. Aware of the team's lack of playoff experience other than Jordin Canada, Dream GM Dan Padover went out and got DeWanna Bonner as a free agent in late August. Bonner has played 100 games in the playoffs, the most in league history.

She joined a stacked lineup that includes Rhyne Howard, Allisha Gray and Angel Reese. That group lifted the Dream to their first playoff win since 2016 when they swept the Washington Mystics.

"I think the pace that they were playing with was really good," Liberty coach Chris DeMarco said. "I think (Bonner) brought a lot of veteran leadership to them, a lot of timely scoring to really settle them into games. I think Howard and Gray are just two really good — or great guards that we have to slow down. When the game gets tough, they kind of put their heads down and kind of take over that scoring."

The Atlanta Dream had one of the best defenses in the league this year, anchored by the WNBA Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese. Atlanta led the league in steals per game (9.1), which it converted to 18.1 points per game. The Dream raised that in the playoffs, scoring 27 points off miscues in their Game 1 win over Washington and getting 23 

They are very active getting into passing lanes, which makes scoring in transition difficult.

The two teams met in the final two games of the regular season with the No. 4 seed on the line, and the Dream won both those contests. Stewart sat out the second game to get some rest heading into the playoffs. Neither team puts much stock in the value of those two games, other than they provided fresh film to both sides from late in the season.

The Dream will play the first two games of the semifinals in State Farm Arena, home of the Atlanta Hawks. Atlanta played six regular-season games at the arena, which seats more than 17,000 fans. The Dream's usual home, the Gateway Center Arena, holds about 3,500. Atlanta played Game 1 of its series against the Mystics at State Farm Arena. If the Dream win in the semifinals, it's unclear what they'll do for the Finals since singer Sombr is performing there the night of Game 3 and the Hawks have their home opener the same evening as Game 4.

title: Yankees’ Gerrit Cole Ties CC Sabathia in MLB History
description: The New York Yankees made the call that folks weren’t sure they would make. Gerrit Cole is going to start Game 1 of the ALDS on Saturday against the Tampa Bay Rays. fullText:
The New York Yankees made the call that folks weren't sure they would make.

Gerrit Cole is going to start Game 1 of the ALDS on Saturday against the Tampa Bay Rays.

Despite struggles late in the season, Cole will get the ball for the game in Tropicana Field that could be crucial for the Yankees to win in what is just a best-of-five series.

The Cole Train comes to Tampa for ALDS Game 1 🚂#RepBX pic.twitter.com/uTSBdY0ba3

— New York Yankees (@Yankees) October 2, 2026

Whether or not the Yankees should be starting Cole will only reveal itself on Saturday.

For now, there is a cool bit of history.

Cole has a long history of starting Game 1 in postseason series.

This will be his ninth Game 1 start (if you also include the single-game Wild Card Series that used to exist).

That's tied for fifth-most all-time, according to MLB Network's Sarah Langs.

Tied with Cole with nine of these starts? CC Sabathia.

In fourth place on the all-time Game 1 starts list is Greg Maddux, who had 11.

There's a tie for second place: Both Clayton Kershaw and Jon Lester started 12 of these games.

And alone in first place, potentially for a long time: Justin Verlander, with 14.

This will be the 9th time Gerrit Cole starts Game 1 of a postseason series (including singular Wild Card Game), tying CC Sabathia for 5th-most all time, behind:

Justin Verlander: 14
 Jon Lester: 12
 Clayton Kershaw: 12
 Greg Maddux: 11 https://t.co/NgopsVMhCQ

— Sarah Langs (@SlangsOnSports) October 2, 2026

Cole finished the 2026 regular season with a 3.61 ERA. That's his worst mark since 2017.

To be fair, it's still a really quality number, but Cole did prove a bit homer-prone late in the year. He also had his lowest strikeout rate (9.3 per nine innings) since that 2017 season, as well.

Cole has been a great playoff pitcher in his career. He has a 2.77 ERA in the postseason.

In the Yankees' 2024 playoff run to the World Series, he had a 2.17 ERA in five games.

Cole's most recent Game 1 start was in Game 1 of the 2024 World Series. He allowed just one run in six innings.

Cole has once faced the Rays in an ALDS Game 1, as well. That was in 2020. He went 6.0 innings and allowed three runs, including two home runs — Randy Arozarena with the first one, and Ji-man Choi with the second.

title: How Sean Durzi Came To Rangers Thanks To Vincent Trocheck

fullText:
Sean Durzi didn't wait long to make his mark with the New York Rangers.

He scored a quick goal on Friday night against the Detroit Red Wings, and he was almost involved in a second before the first period ended — only a miniscule offside overruled it.

Still, it was pretty fast proof in Durzi's Rangers tenure that he's a guy who can make an impact as a defenseman at both ends of the nice.

He's also a player, though, who has flown under the radar heading into a new season. The busy sports ecosystem in New York City can keep a blue-liner relatively unknown until he's actually out there doing things.

Durzi is here now, though, and getting himself noticed.

The Rangers have Vincent Trockeck to help for his arrival.

Durzi came to the Rangers in the Vincent Trocheck trade.

It was an exercise in patience for the Rangers, who had rumors swirling around Trocheck for months and months.

Even when New York traded away Artemi Panarin before the deadline, they opted to hold onto Trocheck. He was still under contract, and so they didn't need to move him yet.

But on July 1, the Rangers did trade Trocheck.

They sent him to the Utah Mammoth for Durzi as well as the prospect Cole Beaudoin and a 2027 third-round pick.

Durzi was coming off a season with five goals and 22 assists (27 points) in 60 games with the Mammoth in 2025-26.

Now, he's trying to do even better for the Rangers as part of a defensive group with a lot of talent.

Durzi is originally from Mississauga in Ontario, Canada.

He went on to play at the junior level in the OHL with the Owen Sound Attack.

The Toronto Maple Leafs drafted Durzi No. 52 overall (second round) in the 2018 NHL Draft.

He actually was a goalie when he first played hockey, but the story goes that his mom preferred he play defenseman, and so that's what he did.

The Maple Leafs traded Durzi before he got near the NHL, sending him to the Los Angeles Kings less than a year after he was drafted.

He played with the Kings through the 2022-23 season, then was traded to the Arizona Coyotes for a 2024 second-round pick.

Arizona moved to Utah, and Durzi was there until he was then sent to the Rangers. Now he's in the Big Apple hoping to make his mark.

title: Will Bears beat the Jets? Our game picks and bold predictions
description: The Chicago Bears battle the New York Jets in Week 4 as Ben Johnson battles Aaron Glenn. Can the Bears improve to 3-1?
fullText:
The Chicago Bears (2-1) are gearing up for a Week 4 matchup against the New York Jets (1-2) on Sunday, where Ben Johnson and Aaron Glenn will face off for the first time since both left the Detroit Lions for head coaching jobs.

The Bears are coming off an impressive 27-7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, where they once again dominated the trenches and made a statement with third-stringer Case Keenum under center amid quarterback injuries. Keenum orchestrated Ben Johnson's offense to perfection, completing 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards and accounting for three total touchdowns. Meanwhile, Chicago's defense had an even better showing in Week 3, holding the Eagles to just seven points, forcing three turnovers and completely shutting them down in the second half.

Now, the focus shifts to a potenital trap game for Chicago, as the Jets have put up a fight against fellow NFC North squads Detroit and Green Bay, before both emerged victorious. Could the Bears be the first NFC North team to win convincingly against New York this season? Our Bears Wire staff certainly thinks so. Here's a look at their game predictions for Bears-Jets in Week 4:

Bold prediction: Bears record 3 takeaways again

The Bears proved they're a good football team with a statement win against the Eagles on Monday night, down their starting and backup quarterbacks. While the Jets aren't the Jets or miserable years past, this is a game that good football teams should win, so I'm expecting nothing less Sunday at Soldier Field. Obviously, the biggest question heading into this game is whether Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum will start at quarterback with Caleb Williams still sidelined. And, honestly, Keenum showed everyone last week that it doesn't really matter. Chicago can win with either Williams, Bagent or Keenum. As long as Ben Johnson is running the show, the Bears are one of the best in the NFL, and he'll have any QB ready to play.

Chicago's run game struggled early against Philadelphia last week, and it won't get any easier against one of the league's top run defenses in New York, which is allowing 87.3 rushing yards per game. D'Andre Swift was a surprise addition to Thursday's injury report with a knee injury, which is certainly worth monitoring, and Kyle Monangai could very well see an uptick in carries. That means Bagent or Keenum might once again have to carry this offense and attack downfield with this array of weapons.

The good -- and still shocking -- news is that the Bears defense has experienced a resurgence after allowing 37 points to the Panthers in Week 1. They're allowing an average 8.0 points per game in the last two contests, and they have an opportunity to continue that hot streak against a Jets team down top running back Breece Hall. Geno Smith is a solid quarterback, but if Chicago can do what they did last week against Jalen Hurts, it could result in another three-takeaway performance.

Bold prediction: Bears shut out Jets in first half

The New York Jets haven't beaten the Chicago Bears in the state of Illinois this millennium, and their first win sure as heck isn't coming with Ben Johnson at the helm. After three weeks, it's becoming clear that the Bears can be a powerhouse in the NFC, and it may not even matter who starts at quarterback. As of this writing, we still don't know whether Case Keenum will get another start with Caleb Williams on the mend or if Tyson Bagent will get the nod. While I'm leaving Bagent, I believe Johnson can carve up this New York defense with either player despite them allowing fewer than 200 total yards in their first couple of games.

These aren't the same old Jets from last year, as they've shown to be quite competitive to start the year. But they're banged up at multiple positions, particularly on offense, and are limited by the effectiveness of Aaron Glenn when it comes to in-game situations. With Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell likely out, Geno Smith will have a tougher time keeping pace with his early-season success. Especially if Olu Fashanu suddenly can't block anyone after allowing three sacks last week against the Detroit Lions.

The Bears are hitting their stride on both offense and defense, and unless another rainstorm engulfs Soldier Field, they will have no trouble taking care of business to start 3-1 for the first time since 2020.

Bold prediction: Dillon Thieneman scores first career TD

This game is tailor-made for the Chicago Bears to leave their impact across the league with Ben Johnson, once again showcasing his offensive excellence as a head coach. The New York Jets are coming in banged up, missing three of their top offensive players, so the defense should have a relatively smoother time in making lifetime on quarterback Geno Smith.

Dillon Thieneman excelled in last week's win over Philadelphia, and I believe the Bears playing at home will create multiple opportunities for the rookie to get his first career touchdown on a takeaway. I will add one more bold prediction, both Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum make appearances in this game. Ben Johnson loves to play to the crowd, and they will be roaring at home with a favorable matchup against the Jets.

Bold prediction: The Bears will run their offense even better this week with a backup QB than last week

The Chicago Bears have one of the best head coaches in the NFL, who also happens to be an elite playcaller. This is his chance to show it again as they face off against the New York Jets. He will have a backup QB under center again, but it shouldn't matter based on the scheming ability of the coach.

The Jets are not a great team, but they have given some scares to NFC North teams so far this year. The Bears will have to come ready to play if they want to make this a game in which they don't feel much pressure.

There is tape out there now to study on what Keenum looks like in his current form with his current team, so that's something for the Bears to think about. Even still, the talent up and down the field and on the sideline should allow them to pull away in the end.

Bold prediction: Chicago will sack Geno Smith at least five times

The New York Jets are not as bad as they have been in previous seasons. They really should have beaten the Green Bay Packers and nearly escaped Week 3 with a win against the Detroit Lions, so they will be competitive in this game as well, at least in the first half. New York only has one turnover in the first three games, so the Bears cannot rely on takeaways on defense to win.

Instead, they need to shut down Geno Smith and the passing attack. New York's running game has struggled and they will most likely be playing without star running back Breece Hall. If the Bears can prevent Smith from finding success against Chicago's defense in the passing game, it will be a long day for the Jets.

Chicago also needs to get pressure on Smith. In the past two games, he has been sacked nine times. The Bears only have seven sacks all year. However, they have the talent to get in the backfield and create havoc. Montez Sweat will have at least one of Chicago's sacks in this game.

Bold prediction: A Bears running back crosses the 100-yard threshold.

The Bears showed a lot against the Eagles on Monday night. They proved they can hang without Caleb Williams at the helm, and their defense continues to prove that they're better than what we saw in Week 1. While the Jets are a much better team than we've come to expect, this is also a matchup that should lean heavily in favor of the Bears if things come together like they did in Week 3.

The run game is what I'm watching. Each of D'Andre Swift & Kyle Monangai have struggled to gain traction since they each exploded back in Week 1. While the Jets have allowed one of the fewest yardage totals on the ground, they're closer to the middle of the pack in yards allowed per rush. Given how crucial it is to Ben Johnson's gameplan, I think that there will be a renewed focus on the ground game to the point where one of Swift (assuming he plays) or Monangai leaves a big impact on the stat sheet.

With the Jets facing a couple of injuries on the offensive side, I think the Bears' defense will continue gaining confidence despite some of their logistical shortcomings. Multiple turnovers again isn't entirely out of the question, and against one of the lower scoring teams in the league, it's completely possible the Jets don't touch the end zone before it's all done on Sunday.

Earlier numbers are from the 2013-14 survey described in Ma et al. (2023). In addition to that, aerial imagery is NYS orthoimagery from summer 2025, and USDA NAIP 2019 for Alley Pond.

fullText:
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said Friday that a woman who alleges she was drugged and raped by multiple members of a Cornell University fraternity in 2024 was "failed" by those obligated to protect her.

Hochul's comments came a day after announcing she had lost faith in the district attorney overseeing the Cornell University rape case and signed an executive order appointing New York Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor to lead the investigation.

"In what world would the police learn from a victim that she'd been literally gang raped while intoxicated by five men in a fraternity house and not elevate those allegations to the district attorney?" Hochul said at a press conference with James in New York. "In what world does the district attorney not even interview her or anyone else involved or even request the full transcript?

"At every turn, she was failed by people and institutions with an obligation to protect her," Hochul said.

James said that the case is "now an active criminal investigation."

"We will review the facts, gather evidence, interview witnesses and, if warranted, pursue prosecutions," James said, adding: "I know that you want answers. I do too."

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten has come under intense scrutiny in recent days over his decision not to prosecute anyone when the initial allegations were made in 2024.

In a civil lawsuit filed last month against the school and seven current and former fraternity members, a former student identified as "Jane Doe" alleged that she was the victim of a "gang rape" at the Chi Phi fraternity on Cornell's Ithaca, N.Y., campus on Oct. 19, 2024. She said she was already intoxicated when she arrived and was given ketamine before and during the alleged assault. She reported the incident to campus police three weeks later.

Van Houten said earlier this week that Jane Doe's sworn statement to police didn't include allegations that she was "drugged against her will or gang raped."

"On the contrary, Jane Doe's statement described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious, and consensual," Van Houten said. "My office obviously did not and could not have based our November 2024 decision on the allegations in a civil lawsuit that would not be filed until nearly two years later."

On Tuesday, CBS New York published excerpts from Jane Doe's Nov. 14, 2024, interview with Cornell police, in which she asserted, "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped."

"Shockingly, those words never made it into the account that the Cornell police sent to prosecutors," Hochul said Friday.

Van Houten said he was not provided with a transcript of her interview before his office decided not to pursue charges.

"I'm going to follow up on this because this is news to me," Van Houten told CBS. "If she had said those words, we certainly would want to have explored that more. Like I said, that wasn't provided to me."

According to ABC News, Jane Doe told the school's investigators that she "felt like bait" on the night of the alleged assault.

"I felt like lions around me," she said during a 2025 hearing. "It just was a totally debilitating place to be in."

The comments were included in a 99-page report prepared by the university as part of its Title IX investigation, per ABC.

The report also included comments from a fraternity member who Cornell's investigation concluded did not engage in the assault but was found responsible for "attempted sexual exploitation."

"I was sorry that maybe if it wasn't consensual and she was victimized, I was sorry for not stopping it," the fraternity members said, according to ABC.

Two of the men have released statements through their lawyers denying they participated in a sexual assault, according to the Associated Press.

Cornell University issued a statement pushing back against claims that the school did not thoroughly punish those involved in the alleged assault.

"Any suggestion that the university did not impose consequential punishments for those involved is false," the university said. "A continuation of the false narrative that there were minimal consequences in this case is irresponsible, will make survivors feel less safe and supported, and will perpetuate the underreporting of sexual assault."

Hochul announced on Wednesday that Cornell had agreed to initiate an independent review of its initial response to the allegations.

The governor also said she would work to close a loophole in New York law, which states that someone who was voluntarily intoxicated cannot claim they were mentally incapacitated during an assault, unless they can show they were "physically helpless" and unable to communicate consent.

"If someone is too intoxicated to consent, it should not matter whether they chose to use drugs or alcohol," Hochul said. "Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape. Period."

On Sept. 14, Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against Cornell University and seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity, alleging that she was the victim of a "gang rape" at the fraternity house when she was incapable of consent — and that the school failed to protect her from "sexual predators" on its campus.

The defendants named in the lawsuit include Cornell, the seven fraternity members, the Chi Phi fraternity, the woman's own sorority, Delta Delta Delta, and an off-campus bar that allegedly served her alcohol.

She is seeking unspecified compensatory and punitive damages resulting from "sustained psychological injuries, severe emotional distress, along with pain and suffering and loss of enjoyment of life."

According to her lawsuit, Jane Doe was a 20-year-old student at the school in October 2024 when she went to visit a friend at the fraternity house on Cornell's Ithaca, N.Y., campus while intoxicated. Shortly after arriving, Jane Doe alleged that she was pressured by two fraternity brothers into snorting what they said was ketamine before sexually assaulting her. One of the men then allegedly sent a message to the fraternity's Snapchat group suggesting that she was available for sex. A screengrab of part of the chat was included in the lawsuit.

According to the complaint, multiple other members of the fraternity showed up, and she was raped for hours.

"The Snapchat was disgusting and vulgar and immoral," Van Houten told ABC News. "But the question that we analyzed was, did Jane Doe consent to what happened? And the law in New York state is clear: That if you are voluntarily intoxicated, or under the influence of drugs such that your judgment is impaired, that does not legally under the penal law constitute your inability to consent."

During the alleged assault, the fraternity members "began pouring lines of Ketamine all over her body and snorting them," according to the complaint.

"At around 5:45 AM, this assault concluded and Plaintiff lost consciousness," the lawsuit stated.

About three weeks later, on Nov. 8, 2024, Jane Doe reported the incident to the university's police department.

According to ABC News, Jane Doe told police in a sworn statement on Nov. 15, 2024, that the incident "felt like coercion," and that at one point she said "no to the foursome" one of the fraternity brothers had proposed. She also stated: "I felt like I was unable to make any decision because of how intoxicated I was."

According to the New York Times, she told Cornell's Title IX investigators that she did not consider herself a victim until she saw the incident being discussed in an online forum.

"Are Chi Phi brothers Crips or Bloods because I hear they have been doing hell Gang Banging?" one user wrote.

"They do drugs and gang r*ped a sophomore," wrote another.

"That's the first time I had ever heard the narrative change that I wasn't a whore and that I was assaulted," Jane Doe told investigators, per the Times.

One of the accused men's lawyers told NBC that his client "made an immature comment on Snapchat," but "did nothing else."

Cornell's months-long Title IX investigation included at least 12 hearings, according to the lawsuit, which said that the accused fraternity members were "afforded the opportunity to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays to Cornell."

Two of the seven accused fraternity members were ultimately expelled, while the others received lesser sanctions, according to the complaint. Jane Doe dropped out of school.

According to CBS, two were suspended for at least two semesters. Cornell denies that students only had to write essays as a disciplinary measure.

Last week, Cornell issued a statement saying that it had concluded its Title IX investigation but would not disclose individual sanctions, citing federal privacy laws.

"The Cornell Office of Civil Rights and the Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards investigated and adjudicated the allegations consistent with university policies. The Xi chapter of Chi Phi fraternity remains barred from our campus," the statement said: "Federal privacy law prohibits Cornell from disclosing specific information regarding individual students and we therefore are unable to make a public statement on any other disciplinary response. Violations of university policies could lead to sanctions up to and including suspension or expulsion. We will respond in detail through the legal process."

The university also pointed out that it launched a task force on campus sexual assault in the wake of the incident and issued a report in March with recommendations for "an environment that fosters sexual health and safety."

"Several of the recommendations have already been implemented, while others are in development with oversight by a university implementation committee," Cornell said.

According to USA Today, more than 1,200 incidents of sexual assault, domestic and dating violence and stalking were reported to Cornell University's Title IX from 2018 through 2024. Of those, 14 cases resulted in suspensions, while seven ended in expulsion or dismissal, per the paper.

"Cornell takes each report seriously and, to the greatest extent possible, honors a complainant's decision not to pursue resolution," Rebecca Valli, a Cornell spokesperson, said in a statement to USA Today. "The university provides support and resources regardless of whether the respondent is subject to our conduct processes, and regardless of whether a complainant consents to an investigation."

The harrowing allegations revealed in Jane Doe's lawsuit prompted reactions from several celebrities, including Florence Pugh, who posted a lengthy response on Instagram calling for men to speak out against sexual violence.

"This is really the moment where we need our men to be as horrified and as sickened as us," Pugh wrote. "You need to be leading conversations about how we change the allowance and complicity of this behaviour as much as we are. How can you expect us to trust that it's 'not all men' when in moments like this, many of you stay quiet?"

In an expletive-laden Instagram post, actor Josh Gad tore into Cornell, seizing on allegations in the civil lawsuit that the fraternity members were required to write essays as part of the adjudication process.

"When we start setting a precedent that our girls and women can be brutally raped, and the resulting disciplinary action is to hand out (checks notes) ESSAYS (like it's Bart Simpson being a lil' rascal), about why it was wrong to brutally violate an innocent girl, we have lost our f***ing minds," Gad wrote.

Toby Morton, a former South Park writer, launched a website, TheCornell7.org, dedicated to holding the school and the accused fraternity members accountable.

"Accountability is coming," Morton wrote on Instagram.

Mariska Hargitay posted a joint statement on Instagram with the Joyful Heart Foundation, which supports survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, and child abuse, with a quote from a scathing editorial by the Cornell Daily Sun.

"Arrest them," Heated Rivalry star Hudson Williams wrote in an Instagram story while sharing a photo of the seven accused men, according to Variety.

"F*** them and f*** Cornell, too!" he added.

At a town hall in Ithaca, N.Y., earlier this week, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a New York Democrat, said that "the culture of rape, sexual assault and pedophilia is protected in elite institutions across the United States, including Cornell."

Ocasio-Cortez recalled her own experience as a freshman at Boston University.

"Within maybe 10 seconds of me walking into a party — at a gym, at a school facility — someone had touched me inappropriately," Ocasio-Cortez said.

"Jane Doe, that survivor, lost her education because you can't stay in school when something like that happens to you," Ocasio-Cortez told the crowd. "She had to lose her education, and those men were protected by an institution and granted an Ivy League degree as a reward. Never again."

The congresswoman said she had a message to Jane Doe and other survivors of sexual assault.

"I want you to know that you are not defined by the things that have happened to you," Ocasio-Cortez said. "You are bigger than that. You are stronger than them. And they will never define you for your entire life. And that you can achieve anything that you want to achieve, from one survivor to another."

fullText:
CNN has obtained newly unsealed police body camera footage showing the arrest of Luigi Mangione inside a McDonald’s in Altoona, Pennsylvania, days after he fatally shot United Healthcare CEO Brian Thompson.

The hours of footage capture officers questioning Mangione at the fast-food restaurant on the morning of December 9, 2024, before he is handcuffed, searched and transported to the police station. The videos show police conducting more thorough searches of Mangione and his belongings at the station, including the moment an officer finds a gun – now known to be the murder weapon – inside his backpack.

This is the first time the videos have been seen outside the courtroom. Some of the footage was played during a dayslong suppression hearing last December, when the defense argued evidence recovered during the arrest should be suppressed because Mangione’s backpack was improperly searched.

New York State Judge Gregory Carro ultimately ruled most of the evidence would be allowed at trial and placed the videos under seal. The judge authorized their release after CNN petitioned for their unsealing following Mangione’s guilty plea to federal charges in August, in which he admitted to fatally shooting Thompson, 50, on a Manhattan sidewalk.

The unsealed videos, taken from body cameras worn by of eight Altoona police officers, show different angles of how the day unfolded as Mangione was approached and questioned by law enforcement, who quickly came to believe he was the suspect tied to the CEO’s killing.

The footage shows Mangione first provided police with a fake ID bearing the name “Mark Rosario” – the same name prosecutors say the shooting suspect used to check into a New York City hostel prior to Thompson’s killing – before later telling law enforcement his real name.

The officers handcuffed Mangione in the fast-food restaurant and searched his pockets and his belongings, including his black backpack, in which they found a gun magazine wrapped in underwear, the videos show.

Mangione was then transported to the police station, where the videos show both he and his bag were further searched. The footage captures the moments police recovered key evidence from the backpack, including a firearm and a notebook with handwritten entries that prosecutors have described as his “manifesto.”

Mangione’s defense attorneys have asked Judge Carro to dismiss the state murder case against him following his guilty plea in federal court late this summer, arguing he would be unlawfully prosecuted under double jeopardy grounds if it proceeds.

The judge has yet to rule on the motion; the parties are due back in state court in December.

"I felt like lions around me," she said during a 2025 hearing, according to ABC News. "It just was a totally debilitating place to be in."

The comments were included in a 99-page report prepared by the university as part of its Title IX investigation, per ABC.

The report also included comments from a fraternity member who Cornell's investigation concluded did not engage in the assault but was found responsible for "attempted sexual exploitation."

"I was sorry that maybe if it wasn't consensual and she was victimized, I was sorry for not stopping it," the fraternity members said, according to ABC.

On Tuesday, CBS New York published excerpts from a Nov. 14, 2024, interview with police, in which Jane Doe asserted, "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped."

Two of the men have released statements through their lawyers denying they participated in a sexual assault, according to the Associated Press.

Van Houten said he was not provided with a transcript of her interview with campus police before his office decided not to pursue charges.

"I'm going to follow up on this because this is news to me," Van Houten told CBS. "If she had said those words, we certainly would want to have explored that more. Like I said, that wasn't provided to me."

In a lengthy statement released on Monday, Van Houten announced that he had reopened the investigation and would present the case to a grand jury. He also sought to explain why he initially decided not to prosecute them.

According to Van Houten, Jane Doe "did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang raped" in a six-page sworn statement to campus police in November 2024.

"On the contrary, Jane Doe's statement described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious, and consensual," Van Houten said. "My office obviously did not and could not have based our November 2024 decision on the allegations in a civil lawsuit that would not be filed until nearly two years later."

Van Houten did not immediately return a request for comment.

Cornell University issued a statement on Monday saying it supported the district attorney's decision to reopen the case while pushing back against claims that the school did not thoroughly punish those involved in the alleged assault.

"Any suggestion that the university did not impose consequential punishments for those involved is false," the university said. "A continuation of the false narrative that there were minimal consequences in this case is irresponsible, will make survivors feel less safe and supported, and will perpetuate the underreporting of sexual assault."

Hochul announced on Wednesday that Cornell had agreed to initiate an independent review of its initial response to the allegations.

On Sept. 14, Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against Cornell University and seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity, alleging that she was the victim of a "gang rape" at the fraternity house when she was incapable of consent — and that the school failed to protect her from "sexual predators" on its campus.

The defendants named in the lawsuit include Cornell, the seven fraternity members, the Chi Phi fraternity, the woman's own sorority, Delta Delta Delta, and an off-campus bar that allegedly served her alcohol.

She is seeking unspecified compensatory and punitive damages resulting from "sustained psychological injuries, severe emotional distress, along with pain and suffering and loss of enjoyment of life."

According to her lawsuit, Jane Doe was a 20-year-old student at the school in October 2024 when she went to visit a friend at the fraternity house on Cornell's Ithaca, N.Y., campus while intoxicated. Shortly after arriving, Jane Doe alleged that she was pressured by two fraternity brothers into snorting what they said was ketamine before sexually assaulting her. One of the men then allegedly sent a message to the fraternity's Snapchat group suggesting that she was available for sex. A screengrab of part of the chat was included in the lawsuit.

According to the complaint, multiple other members of the fraternity showed up, and she was raped for hours.

"The Snapchat was disgusting and vulgar and immoral," Van Houten told ABC News. "But the question that we analyzed was, did Jane Doe consent to what happened? And the law in New York state is clear: That if you are voluntarily intoxicated, or under the influence of drugs such that your judgment is impaired, that does not legally under the penal law constitute your inability to consent."

During the alleged assault, the fraternity members "began pouring lines of Ketamine all over her body and snorting them," according to the complaint.

"At around 5:45 AM, this assault concluded and Plaintiff lost consciousness," the lawsuit stated.

About three weeks later, on Nov. 8, 2024, Jane Doe reported the incident to the university's police department.

According to ABC News, Jane Doe told police in a sworn statement on Nov. 15, 2024, that the incident "felt like coercion," and that at one point she said "no to the foursome" one of the fraternity brothers had proposed. She also stated: "I felt like I was unable to make any decision because of how intoxicated I was."

According to the New York Times, she told Cornell's Title IX investigators that she did not consider herself a victim until she saw the incident being discussed in an online forum.

"Are Chi Phi brothers Crips or Bloods because I hear they have been doing hell Gang Banging?" one user wrote.

"They do drugs and gang r*ped a sophomore," wrote another.

"That's the first time I had ever heard the narrative change that I wasn't a whore and that I was assaulted," Jane Doe told investigators, per the Times.

One of the accused men's lawyers told NBC that his client "made an immature comment on Snapchat," but "did nothing else."

Cornell's months-long Title IX investigation included at least 12 hearings, according to the lawsuit, which said that the accused fraternity members were "afforded the opportunity to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays to Cornell."

Two of the seven accused fraternity members were ultimately expelled, while the others received lesser sanctions, according to the complaint. Jane Doe dropped out of school.

According to CBS, two were suspended for at least two semesters. Cornell denies that students only had to write essays as a disciplinary measure.

Last week, Cornell issued a statement saying that it had concluded its Title IX investigation but would not disclose individual sanctions, citing federal privacy laws.

"The Cornell Office of Civil Rights and the Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards investigated and adjudicated the allegations consistent with university policies. The Xi chapter of Chi Phi fraternity remains barred from our campus," the statement said: "Federal privacy law prohibits Cornell from disclosing specific information regarding individual students and we therefore are unable to make a public statement on any other disciplinary response. Violations of university policies could lead to sanctions up to and including suspension or expulsion. We will respond in detail through the legal process."

The university also pointed out that it launched a task force on campus sexual assault in the wake of the incident and issued a report in March with recommendations for "an environment that fosters sexual health and safety."

"Several of the recommendations have already been implemented, while others are in development with oversight by a university implementation committee," Cornell said.

According to USA Today, more than 1,200 incidents of sexual assault, domestic and dating violence and stalking were reported to Cornell University's Title IX from 2018 through 2024. Of those, 14 cases resulted in suspensions, while seven ended in expulsion or dismissal, per the paper.

"Cornell takes each report seriously and, to the greatest extent possible, honors a complainant's decision not to pursue resolution," Rebecca Valli, a Cornell spokesperson, said in a statement to USA Today. "The university provides support and resources regardless of whether the respondent is subject to our conduct processes, and regardless of whether a complainant consents to an investigation."

The harrowing allegations revealed in Jane Doe's lawsuit prompted reactions from several celebrities, including Florence Pugh, who posted a lengthy response on Instagram calling for men to speak out against sexual violence.

"This is really the moment where we need our men to be as horrified and as sickened as us," Pugh wrote. "You need to be leading conversations about how we change the allowance and complicity of this behaviour as much as we are. How can you expect us to trust that it's 'not all men' when in moments like this, many of you stay quiet?"

In an expletive-laden Instagram post, actor Josh Gad tore into Cornell, seizing on allegations in the civil lawsuit that the fraternity members were required to write essays as part of the adjudication process.

"When we start setting a precedent that our girls and women can be brutally raped, and the resulting disciplinary action is to hand out (checks notes) ESSAYS (like it's Bart Simpson being a lil' rascal), about why it was wrong to brutally violate an innocent girl, we have lost our f***ing minds," Gad wrote.

Toby Morton, a former South Park writer, launched a website, TheCornell7.org, dedicated to holding the school and the accused fraternity members accountable.

"Accountability is coming," Morton wrote on Instagram.

Mariska Hargitay posted a joint statement on Instagram with the Joyful Heart Foundation, which supports survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, and child abuse, with a quote from a scathing editorial by the Cornell Daily Sun.

"Arrest them," Heated Rivalry star Hudson Williams wrote in an Instagram story while sharing a photo of the seven accused men, according to Variety.

"F*** them and f*** Cornell, too!" he added.

At a town hall in Ithaca, N.Y., earlier this week, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a New York Democrat, said that "the culture of rape, sexual assault and pedophilia is protected in elite institutions across the United States, including Cornell."

"Jane Doe, that survivor, lost her education because you can't stay in school when something like that happens to you," Ocasio-Cortez told the crowd. "She had to lose her education, and those men were protected by an institution and granted an Ivy League degree as a reward. Never again."

She also had a message to Jane Doe and other survivors of sexual assault.

"I want you to know that you are not defined by the things that have happened to you," Ocasio-Cortez said. "You are bigger than that. You are stronger than them. And they will never define you for your entire life. And that you can achieve anything that you want to achieve, from one survivor to another."

title: New details emerge in Cornell rape case as Letitia James takes over investigation

fullText:
New York State Attorney General Letitia James will be taking over as special prosecutor in the case alleging sexual assault at Cornell University, Gov. Kathy Hochul announced Thursday, saying she “lost faith” in the district attorney’s ability to oversee it.

The announcement comes as new details have emerged this week about the alleged gang rape of then-student Jane Doe in a room at the Chi Phi fraternity house in 2024, including what she told campus police about the alleged assault.

“New information has raised serious questions about how this case was handled, and I’ve lost faith in the Tompkins County DA’s ability to fairly oversee it,” Hochul said in a statement. “The young woman at the center of this case deserves to know that every fact will be examined and justice pursued.”

James will now have the power to investigate the incident and, if warranted, prosecute any offenses and present evidence to a grand jury. Cornell told CNN Thursday it supports the governor’s decision.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten has repeatedly told CNN that his office never received more than the Snapchat messages and a six-page investigative report before deciding not to bring charges in the case.

In the report, Doe she recounted being hit and feeling emotionally coerced into sexual activity while intoxicated.

She made a more explicit accusation of rape in a November 2024 interview with campus police – the transcript of which Van Houten told CNN his office never received.

Cornell has said police followed protocol and shared “all investigatory information” with the DA. But many questions remain about the initial investigation and what the county district attorney knew about the allegations. Here’s what we know:

Snapchat messages exchanged during the alleged assault in a group chat titled “Chi Phi Actives” include a photo of then-student Jane Doe in a room at the fraternity house, according to images of the chain obtained by CNN.

The conversations taking place on the fast-erasing messaging app suggest other photos or videos might have been recovered had there been a more thorough criminal investigation, according to a source close to the case.

CNN has previously reported messages in the group chat that stated “free p*ssy” upstairs and asked, “Shop still open?”

Additional images of messages obtained by CNN include a reference to one member “laying rn,” and other members asking, “are you guys at least naked?” and stating, “Like you can walk in and whip it out rn.”

In the three weeks between when the former student was allegedly gang raped to her describing the night to campus police, Doe appeared to wrestle with shame and her stance had evolved on whether an assault took place, according to records obtained exclusively by the New York Times and corroborated by Doe’s attorney.

In an article published Thursday, the Times cited documents from the university’s formal Title IX investigation that shed new light on how Doe initially viewed the night’s events, discussed them with her roommates and communicated with some of the men before she reported her allegations to university police.

“Ms. Doe’s internal processing went from denial, to shame and ultimately acceptance that she had been raped by people that she thought were her friends,” her attorney, Thomas P. Giuffra, told CNN Thursday. “Her reactions were a textbook reaction to trauma.”

CNN has not seen the Title IX filings, which are generally confidential and restricted to the parties involved.

Cornell’s investigation yielded hundreds of pages of emails, text messages, photos and interviews with Doe, her friends and six of the seven men she accused, according to the Times. The files also included an extensive transcript of the original police interviews with Doe, the Times reported.

After the alleged gang rape at Chi Phi fraternity that began on October 19, 2024, Doe recounted the night’s events to her roommates without identifying herself as a rape victim, the Times reported, citing the files.

The following narrative comes from the Times’ review of the Title IX files it obtained:

Doe reportedly told her two roommates the day she returned home that she had consumed ketamine and had sex with multiple men. One roommate told investigators that Jane Doe did not use the word “rape” or “assault” yet.

One roommate said she could not remember Doe saying yes to anything that occurred while another roommate said it appeared Doe was “in shock,” the roommate told investigators, “not really understanding the gravity of what she was saying.”

The next day, Doe reportedly spoke with her sorority big sister, who later told investigators “what she was going through is that she had not yet processed what had happened.”

Doe had also communicated with at least two of the men she later accused of sexual assault, according to the Times.

One reportedly sent Doe a text message which said: “I just wanted to apologize for how things went down the other night.” The sender said he and another male who was allegedly involved felt terrible and too under the influence of drugs and alcohol to “shut it down and kick people out before it got way out of hand.”

Doe replied to the man reassuringly, the Times reported, saying “non of the sexual stuff was illegal.”

But once she came to terms with what happened, she went to a health professional a few days after the incident, Doe’s attorney told CNN.

A heavily redacted, 99-page document obtained by CNN summarizes key evidence included in a Cornell disciplinary panel’s decision.

“I felt like bait. I felt like lions around me. It was just a totally debilitating place to be in,” Doe told Cornell investigators in a hearing months after her alleged assault at the Chi Phi fraternity, according to the panel’s findings.

While CNN has been unable to view the entire document due to redactions, it describes the heavy presence of ketamine at the fraternity house on the night of the alleged assault, as well as Doe’s reported state of mind at certain points.

Doe described the effects of ketamine as “vague consciousness,” according to the panel’s decision.

“You look like an operating human being… You don’t look dead or asleep necessarily. So, lights are on, but nobody’s home. Your brain is not functioning at its proper level,” she said.

Details previously reported by CNN describe Doe telling police she consumed ketamine on the night of the assault.

The panel’s decision also cites a recorded phone call Doe had with one of the defendants in early November 2024, where they discussed ketamine and other substances they took as the initial sexual activity began on the night of the alleged assault.

Doe started recording her phone calls after the alleged assault so she could have a “reference to the limited information she was receiving,” as she sought to process what happened, according to Giuffra.

Doe also recalled being “naked” in a fraternity house bed at some point during the night of the alleged assault while two men stood by, according to the decision. “They felt more like voyeurs than anything,” she said in a November interview with investigators.

A few days after the incident, Doe went to Cornell Health to get treated for a urinary tract infection and to get tested for sexually transmitted diseases, her attorney said.

“Ms. Doe disclosed to the treating health care professional that she contracted the UTI in a ‘traumatic way,’” Giuffra said about the October 22 visit.

“Ms. Doe’s disclosure warranted further inquiry, including a rape kit, consultation of medical professionals trained to deal with rape cases and a physical exam to document her injuries,” her attorney said. “Inexplicably, all the medical professional did was to advise Ms. Doe to ‘speak with somebody.’”

CNN asked the university for comment on Giuffra’s claims against Cornell Health. “At this time, we have no new information” beyond Cornell’s previous statements about the case, a Cornell spokesperson said Thursday.

Giuffra said Cornell Health failed to act during a critical window for obtaining evidence.

“Timing is vital for rape kits because DNA evidence is lost over time,” the attorney said. “Critically, two days after the assault, a rape kit would likely have revealed DNA which would have been significant information for a criminal investigation. However this was not offered or suggested.”

Doe’s attorney said he doesn’t know whether the trove of details from the Title IX investigation was ever given to Cornell police.

“I believe that the information was not, because what is contained in the proceedings is evidence of several crimes being committed with excellent supporting evidence,” Giuffra said in a statement to CNN.

Giuffra said his office did not give the documents to the Times – but he’s grateful someone did.

“There are strict privacy policies in Title IX proceedings and access to these documents are limited to school officials, involved parties and their lawyers,” Giuffra said in his statement. “I want it to be clear that we were not responsible for leaking these documents.”

But “frankly, I am glad it was leaked,” he said. “It just shows how badly this whole tragedy was handled from all sides. Even medical providers did not do the right thing.”

In the weeks after the alleged gang rape, interviews with Doe, her roommates and her sorority big sister describe a 20-year-old sophomore realizing the severity of the night’s events and understanding them as an alleged assault, according to the Times.

The documents reportedly detail how rumors about the alleged gang rape led her to fear reputational damage and left her humiliated.

It was an evolution of thought complicated by Doe’s history as a sexual assault survivor, the Times reports, citing the documents. In the six-page summary signed by Doe to police, she described having a prior “traumatic experience” regarding sexual intercourse.

After the alleged rape, Doe saw comments on an online forum about Greek life about Chi Phi brothers drugging and gang raping a sophomore, which she later told investigators: “That’s the first time I had ever heard the narrative change that I wasn’t a whore and that I was assaulted,” the Times reported.

On November 3, Doe texted one of the men, explicitly saying that what happened on that October night was not consensual. According to the Times, she wrote: “let’s be clear that 90% of what happened that night was not consensual. i was given more key than i can remember,” using a shorthand for ketamine, “and i know that i told u i felt uncomfortable and i didn’t know anyone in the room.”

Before going to campus police, Doe reportedly collected evidence, including photos of the bruises on her body allegedly caused by one of the men hitting her. She also had not washed the dress to save as potential evidence, the Times reports.

On November 7, Doe went to an emergency room in Ithaca, where Cornell is located, and requested a rape kit, the Times reported, citing the documents.

In a 2024 statement to Cornell police, obtained by CNN from a source familiar with the investigation, Doe recounted arriving at the Chi Phi fraternity house and dancing with one person who asked if she would be interested in participating in a threesome. Doe told police she was “pretty ok” with aspects of an initial encounter, but that later in the night she did not consent to other sexual activities, according to the six-page statement.

“I felt like I was unable to make any decisions because of how intoxicated I was,” she said in the statement. Doe said she felt like her overall intoxication level at one point was about an “8 out of 10” — which she said was the most intoxicated she had been in her life.

She described being “pretty incapacitated,” feeling uncomfortable, swatting one man’s hand away several times and being “horrified” as more men entered the room they were in. She said she “finally gave in” to one later encounter after she was asked “to have sex so many times,” according to the statement.

“To me that felt like coercion,” she said in the statement. “Also, I felt like due to my intoxication, they should have known how intoxicated I was based on how I was slurring my words.”

Doe made a more explicit accusation of rape in a separate document, according to CNN affiliate WCBS. The station obtained a transcript of a November 2024 interview with campus police from a source.

“I can say with 100% confidence I was raped,” Doe said in the transcript, according to WCBS.

CNN has not seen the transcript and has asked Cornell for a copy but has not heard back. The transcript is a separate document from the six-page statement that was submitted by the university.

Beyond alleged emotional pressure, Doe told police in the statement she was physically hit and remembered feeling hurt. “One hit in particular sent a sharp pain through me,” she said. The student also described noticing bruising on her body the following day.

Doe also said she “had become extremely uncomfortable with how this night was turning out” and thought, “if I passed out and the men had sex with me, then they could be charged with Rape,” the statement reads.

Doe told police she remembered consuming a “heavy amount” of ketamine, smoking marijuana and having “various things” poured on her body. She said she initially agreed to having drugs consumed off her body while feeling “extremely tired” but “couldn’t tell what they were pouring on me.”

Doe reported the alleged incident to Cornell police on November 8, 2024, weeks after the alleged assault, according to a civil complaint filed last month. In the days following the alleged incident, she was “traumatized, numb and unable to function or accept the horror of what had happened,” her attorney told CNN.

Cornell’s internal investigation revealed Doe planned to return to the fraternity house the following week for a Halloween party, according to two sources familiar with the school’s Title IX investigation.

But a fraternity official spoke with Doe before the party and advised her not to go, one of the sources told CNN. The source said fraternity members, Doe’s friends and Doe herself mentioned this in their testimonies during Cornell’s investigation.

“It was all part of her processing what had happened. She was still in the denial stage,” her attorney said. “She could not accept what happened to her.”

In the following days, Doe reported the October incident to Cornell police, according to her lawsuit.

Van Houten told CNN his office was not given the interview transcript before deciding no charges should be filed in the investigation.

The DA told CNN on Wednesday morning that the university had still not provided his office with the transcript. CNN had also reached out to Van Houten about whether it received the Title IX filings.

The DA said it was Doe’s six-page statement that determined no charges should be filed, adding, “Multiple prosecutors and criminal investigators reviewed Jane Doe’s statement and correctly determined the alleged facts as set forth in the statement do not constitute a crime.”

Van Houten said he learned of the more explicit allegation made in the interview when he was contacted by WCBS on Tuesday evening and said his office will be investigating the reported statements “fully.”

When reached by CNN about the DA’s comments, a Cornell University spokesperson did not specifically address the transcript but said it “shared all investigatory information” with the DA’s office.

The university likely did not break any laws if it did neglect to share all relevant documents with the DA, said former prosecutor Gary Galperin. But he said not sharing all documents would violate “all principles of what’s logical and decent.”

The DA’s comments Wednesday raised new questions about what law enforcement knew in the weeks after the alleged assault and why no criminal charges were filed.

“It is a case that, clearly, just on the face of her statement, is so complex and so nuanced,” former Westchester County District Attorney Mimi Rocah said

“If you’re an investigator trying to get at the truth, as this DA office should have been, they should have sought more information,” she added.

Van Houten canceled his scheduled appearance on CNN Wednesday evening, saying, “At this time I need to shift my focus to the investigation and to pursuing the additional evidence that has recently come to light.”

He said his office will keep the public informed of developments in the investigation and any action of the Tompkins County Grand Jury.

After Doe’s allegations, “Cornell established the Presidential Task Force on Campus Sexual Assault, comprising faculty, staff, and students, in early 2025,” the university said.

“Our goal is not simply to respond appropriately when sexual misconduct is reported, but to build a community in which sexual violence is prevented, people feel safe coming forward, those who do are supported, and individuals found responsible are held accountable.”

But some Cornell students who were on campus in 2024 said the university’s response hasn’t been enough.

“The main problem I see in the university’s response … is the lack of ownership,” said Hayden Watkins, executive vice president of the Cornell Student Assembly.

He also said the school’s task force on campus sexual assault is not representative.

“There’s been very little student voice throughout this entire process,” Watkins said. “That task force included roughly 20 individuals, but only two people were undergraduate students.”

The unfolding details of Jane Doe’s case have sparked renewed attention to the ongoing topic of sexual assault awareness and prevention on college campuses.

Doe’s attorney has said Cornell expelled two of the seven accused students while the others received lesser punishments, including suspensions, workshops or written assignments.

Cornell has countered that claim, saying “none of the individuals charged were offered the opportunity to write essays as a sole consequence of their involvement.”

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said Cornell has agreed to an outside investigation to “determine whether Cornell met every obligation to protect its students and pursue justice,” she told CNN. The university confirmed that it agreed to the investigation and declined to provide further details.

The Chi Phi national fraternity said Wednesday that it condemns sexual assault and drug and alcohol abuse, and three days after Doe filed a police report, the fraternity chapter “voted unanimously to remove the accused members from its rolls” and “recommended that our national fraternity permanently expel them,” which it said the fraternity’s Grand Council did in a subsequent meeting.

“These actions went beyond anything the law or Cornell University required of us,” the fraternity added in the statement.

The school also said it had closed that chapter of the Chi Phi fraternity in 2024, and that the chapter remains barred from campus.

It is unclear if any of the accused men are still Cornell students.

Help is available: For help in the US, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673 or chat 24/7 on online.rainn.org.

CNN’s Holly Yan, Chris Boyette, Rebekah Riess, Cindy Von Quednow, Avni Trivedi, Pamela Brown, Jake Tapper and Jeff Winter contributed to this report.

A student alleged that seven fraternity members sexually assaulted her in 2024.

In a statement, James said she is “ready to lead a process New Yorkers can trust, guided by the facts and the law.”

“Every New Yorker deserves to know that when they report a crime, it will be investigated fully and fairly. The Governor has entrusted my office with this investigation, and we do not take that responsibility lightly,” James said.

The appointment of James as special prosecutor comes five days after Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said he would reopen the investigation into the former student's allegations.

Late last month, the former student, listed as Jane Doe, filed a civil lawsuit alleging that she was drugged, assaulted and "gang raped" by seven former and current members of the Chi Phi fraternity at Cornell.

Van Houten said in a statement on Sunday that his office ​was considering whether to bring criminal charges related to the incident, though he said the allegations in the civil complaint are "dramatically different" than the woman's statement to police two years ago.

In an interview with ABC News, Van Houten acknowledged that he relied on the investigation conducted by Cornell Police and said his office didn't "independently investigate" the allegations.

Hochul called for the outside review, saying the allegations raised "serious questions about Cornell campus culture" and whether the university is doing all it can to protect students.

"Cornell shares Governor Hochul’s commitment to addressing campus culture issues, which affect universities across the nation and New York. We are committed to continuing to work with state officials to advance student safety and wellbeing,” a Cornell spokesperson said in a statement provided to ABC News.

title: J.J. McCarthy hits the ground running with New York Giants
description: Quarterback J.J. McCarthy has been with the New York Giants for mere days, but he's already staying late and getting up to speed.
fullText:
It didn't take long for quarterback J.J. McCarthy to hit the ground running with his new team, the New York Giants, after coming over in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings on Monday.

"I mean, it's been good to get him here. I'm excited about it," head coach John Harbaugh told reporters about McCarthy's arrival on Wednesday. "It's an opportunity for us to improve our team, one little way maybe. And who knows where it goes or where it doesn't go.

"But yeah, I've seen a guy. I mean, he had a really good practice. Seems like he picked things up we asked him to pick up really well. Was in here late, early. Studying, learning. Has a really good football foundation, all that kind of stuff. And that's exciting. It's another good football player at an important position."

McCarthy will be playing catch-up, taking a crash course in the Giants' offense with the hope that he can contribute sooner rather than later. For now, he'll back up Jameis Winston, who himself is still acclimating to his new position.

Winston was asked for his first impression of McCarthy, who was wearing jersey No. 18 on Wednesday.

"I think he's a good kid, and I'm happy to have anyone that's my teammate," Winston said after practice. "Obviously, we share -- we won the national championship. We share (that) he got coached by a Harbaugh. I'm getting coached by a Harbaugh right now. We share that -- those similarities. But he's curious. He wants to be great. I think anybody that gets the opportunity to come to a new organization with a fresh start wants to make an impact.

"What I want for myself, I want for everyone. So, if he wants to join the routine, he's definitely welcome."

Harbaugh said Winston would be the starter until further notice.

Winston, an 11-year NFL veteran, knows things can change quickly. He said he needs to play his best to stay in the role.

The Giants host the Arizona Cardinals this Sunday at MetLife Stadium. Winston will get the start, but many eyes will be on this situation over the next few weeks.
